chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the sacrificial camels are many, he stands between two of them, then marks the right one, then the left one. And he does not mark until he is ready for the Ihram, because when he marks, and yokes, and decorates, the Ihram becomes obligatory upon him, and it is in the status of the Talbiyyah.

key_terms.أَشْعَرَ: To mark or brand the animal, specifically on the right and left sides
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: The recitation of 'Labbayk' (Here I am) during Hajj
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: The sacred state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْبُدْنُ: Sacrificial camels or animals designated for sacrifice
key_terms.جَلَّلَ: To decorate or cover the animal with a cloth
key_terms.قَلَّدَ: To yoke or place the neck-ring on the animal

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual significance of marking sacrificial animals before Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the preparatory rites for the sacrificial camel (Hady), emphasizing that the physical acts of marking (Ish'ar), yoking (Taqleed), and adorning (Jall) serve as the definitive trigger for the obligation of Ihram. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes a parallel between the ritual preparation of the animal and the pilgrim's verbal declaration, underscoring that the commitment to the sacred state is sealed through these tangible preparations before the actual entry into the Miqat.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When there are many camels, stand in what is between the two, then mark the right side, then the left, but do not mark it ever until you are ready for the Ihraan, because when one marks, and yokes, and decorates, the Ihraam would be Obligatory upon him, and it is at the status of the Talbiyya’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When there are many al-Budn, one stands in between the two, then marks on the right and then on the left. Never mark before you are ready to assume the state of Ihram because when it is decorated, something placed around its neck or marked, assuming the state of Ihram becomes obligatory upon you and it is like Talbiyah.’”
